extracted.intended_audience: scholars, textual editors, and readers of a scholarly edition of The Spectator (editors of historical literary texts)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and editorial principles for producing a scholarly reprint of The Spectator: how to collate issues, present variants, handle spelling/punctuation/typography, and place translations, notes, and appendices to preserve authorial text and aid readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint the text as the authors left it
rubrics_metrics.description: This volume reprints for the first time in the present century the text of the 'Spectator' as its authors left it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The original text is given precisely as it was left after revision by its authors; the Essays, as revised by their authors for permanent use, form the main text of the present volume. The edition shows at the same time the amount and character of the revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark sentences added in the reprint with square brackets
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences added in the reprint are placed between square brackets [ ], without any appended note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions introduced by the editor in the reprint are explicitly bracketed inline so readers can identify material not present in the original daily issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show omitted or altered words by bracketing with footnote original
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences omitted, or words altered, are shown by bracketing the revised version, and giving the text as it stood in the original daily issue within corresponding brackets as a foot-note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the permanent (revised) text differs from the original daily number, the revised wording is bracketed in the main text and the original wording is given in a footnote within corresponding brackets, enabling reconstruction of the first-issue text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve original spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: As the few differences between good spelling in Queen Anne's time and good spelling now are never of a kind to obscure the sense of a word, or lessen the enjoyment of the reader, it has been thought better to make the reproduction perfect, and thus show not only what Steele and Addison wrote, but how they spelt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not modernize historic spellings; retain authorial orthography so readers can see period spelling practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore authors' punctuation and use of capitals
rubrics_metrics.description: While restoring to their style the proper harmony of their own methods of punctuating, and their way of sometimes getting emphasis by turning to account the use of capitals, which in their hands was not wholly conventional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid modernizing punctuation or 'correcting' the authors' punctuation/capitalization choices; where modernization has been done by earlier editors it may be counted as a defect and should be reversed except in cases of clear misprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduce original typographical disposition (folio numbers, italics, special marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: The original folio numbers have been followed also in the use of _italics_ [_shown between underscored thus_] and other little details of the disposition of the type; for example, in the reproduction of those rows of single inverted commas, which distinguish what a correspondent called the parts 'laced down the side with little c's.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve typographical features such as folio numeration, italics conventions, and distinctive punctuation/quotation rows when practicable; note when certain formatting details cannot be reproduced in a particular file or medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place translations of mottos and Latin quotations in an Appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation of the mottos and Latin quotations, which Steele and Addison deliberately abstained from giving, and which, as they were since added, impede and sometimes confound and contradict the text, are here placed in a body at the end, for those who want them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not insert translations into the head of essays where authors omitted them; provide translations in a dedicated appendix so they do not disrupt or contradict the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include appendix of original advertisements when illustrative
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a short Appendix also of advertisements taken from the original number of the 'Spectator', and a few others, where they seem to illustrate some point in the text, will be found among the notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduce contemporary paratext (advertisements) selectively in an appendix when they illuminate the context or interpretation of items in the main text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add explanatory notes to clarify authorship, allusions, and manners
rubrics_metrics.description: In the large number of notes here added to a revision of those bequeathed to us by Percy and Calder, the object has been to give information which may contribute to some nearer acquaintance with the writers of the book, and enjoyment of allusions to past manners and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide historical, biographical, and cultural notes aimed at helping modern readers understand personal allusions, contemporary manners, and references that would otherwise be obscure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use earlier annotated editions and indicate editorial provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: These [Percy and Calder's] notes are those of which the substance has run through all subsequent editions. ... Percy's notes have a P. attached to them, and Dr. Calder's are signed 'Annotator.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate useful material from prior editors (noting their sigla) and clearly mark which notes/annotations derive from which earlier editor to preserve provenance and allow evaluation of editorial interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collate daily issues, revised octavos, and last pre-death edition
rubrics_metrics.description: The papers as they first appeared in the daily issue of a penny (and after the stamp was imposed two-penny) folio half-sheet, have been closely compared with the first issue in guinea octavos, for which they were revised, and with the last edition that appeared before the death of Steele.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically collate all relevant states (first daily issue, revised octavo permanent text, and later editions) to identify authorial revisions, compositor errors, and later corruptions; present both the revised (main) text and apparatus showing original readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow reader to reconstruct original daily text by substitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Thus the reader has here both the original texts of the 'Spectator'. ... But if the words or passages in brackets be omitted; the words or passages in corresponding foot-notes,--where there are such foot-notes,--being substituted for them; the text becomes throughout that of the 'Spectator' as it first came out in daily numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear mechanism (brackets + footnotes) enabling the text to be converted into the original daily-number text by substituting bracketed/referenced material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid willful alteration and unjustified 'corrections' of style
rubrics_metrics.description: If the present edition has its own share of misprints and oversights, at least it inherits none; and it contains no wilful alteration of the text. ... editors of another 'understanding age' have also taken upon themselves by many a little touch to correct Addison's style or grammar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from emendations that alter authorial style or grammar unless justified by clear manuscript or authorial evidence; prefer to note suspected 'corrections' rather than silently change them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document the amount and character of revisions and misprints
rubrics_metrics.description: A good recent edition contains in the first 18 papers, which are a fair sample of the whole, 88 petty variations from the proper text (at that rate, in the whole work more than 3000) apart from the recasting of the punctuation, which is counted as a defect only in two instances, where it has changed the sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify and describe the scope of textual corruptions and editorial changes so users can assess the editorial state of the text; note where punctuation changes alter sense and treat them as defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ and extend a reliable index for reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Finally, from the 'General Index to the Spectators, &c.,' published as a separate volume in 1760, there has been taken what was serviceable, and additions have been made to it with a desire to secure for this edition of the 'Spectator' the advantages of being handy for reference as well as true to the real text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reuse authoritative indexing resources, augment them as needed, and produce an index that supports both referencing and fidelity to the text.
